correctness.rationale: Identify the rook graph with line graph L(K_m,n). Edge-set connectedness becomes connectivity of its occupied bipartite subgraph; domination iff all rows or all columns occupied. Minimality excludes cycles and both shores simultaneously full; if rows are full and columns are partial, occupied columns must have degree >=2. Conversely every such tree is deletion-minimal by losing an occupied row or disconnecting the chosen edges. Monotonicity and spanning-tree pruning upgrade single-deletion minimality to full inclusion-minimality. Bipartite Pruefer code has m^(c−1) row choices and c! S(m−1,c) surjective column words, proving both sums. Positive Stirling supports give cardinality intervals and missing interval n>=2m. Independent exhaustive graph check covers 5 small rectangles including (3,4).
residual_risks: Bounded finite verification alone cannot prove the universal claim; symbolic proof reconstruction is the principal support.

value.rationale: An exact all-size coefficientwise enumeration and sharp possible-cardinality gap of inclusion-minimal connected domination sets in a canonical Cartesian-product graph family. It distinguishes inclusion-minimal from minimum and from all connected dominating subsets, and may be used in graph census and extremal connected domination.
residual_risks: Mathematical usefulness is confined to the hypotheses and boundaries of the stated claim.

final_claim: For all rook graphs K_m square K_n, m,n>=2, all inclusion-minimal connected dominating subsets are enumerated by two disjoint families of occupied bipartite trees with one fully covered shore and all opposite occupied degrees >=2, giving the exact two-sum Stirling-number polynomial and cardinality gap iff n>=2m after m<=n.
limitations: An unindexed line-graph domination or bipartite-tree enumerator might contain an equivalent all-parameter formula; priority cannot be certified by negative search.
